note: Keyboard face and skin cases (shared/types/keyboardFace.ts). A skin is authored on the SERVER and expanded into the key tree config.ts already builds; the phone ships primitives only and never sees a skin object. These cases check both ends: what the expansion may produce, and what a renderer must refuse even if it somehow arrives.

faceCases.why: The plainest print: a legend in a bundled face. The key keeps insertKey, shift casing, the accent tray and the fast in-place re-title.
A second legend and a corner glyph: what a long press would give, printed where a person can see it.
A vector print in the shared grammar. This is the one new mark shape in this build; rect, line, circle and bars already ship on the mic key.

faceCases.constraint: at most 3 keys in one config
faceCases.why: The motion language that already ships on the mic key, unchanged: numbers only, no I/O, bounded repeats, unknown means 0. It already stops under Reduce Motion, is already capped in frames per second, and already turns a bad program into a still picture. This spec does not widen it, which is what keeps the build inside App Review 2.5.2.

faceCases.at: press.x / press.y / since.press in the program context
faceCases.why: There is NO press position in a program's context. A key position is a letter, and prints do not need it: giving a program the press point would be the one way a skin could learn something about typing.

Face art by content hash, from the compiled-in art host, listed in skin.manifest and fetched in ONE batch when the config arrives. It is decoded at the key's frame size x scale (never above 160 px), not at kb.images.maxEdgePx, which is in POINTS and would mean 768 px on a 3x phone.

The art host is a COMPILED-IN allow-list in both TulmiImageLoaders (exactly api.x0bot.com and api.tailzu.space, https only). Today a config push could make the keyboard fetch from any host; that is a T0 fix, not a T1 nicety. A skin can never carry a tracking pixel.

Art is the BARE manifest name, <sha256>@<scale>.png, even when the URL names our own host. Each phone builds the address from its own compiled host, so no host ever travels in a config and a binary in the field cannot be pointed anywhere new. The server's lint once kept only the last / segment of this, which let a foreign host through the check and then be silently dropped by both phones.

An icon is sf, asset or emoji. There is no url form: a picture goes through `art`, by content hash. The iOS face already reads only the three, so a url icon could only ever be a fetch we did not mean to allow.

The renderer reads ONLY the cache. A file that was not in the manifest was never prefetched, so drawing it would mean a fetch during a session — which would tie a request to a keystroke. Missing art means the flat colour for that session.

faceCases.at: an animated GIF or APNG in a face
faceCases.why: No animated raster in a face in format 1: thirty animated keys is a different class of cost from one mic key. Use a mark with `program` for motion, which is budgeted and capped at 3 keys.

THE FIRST LAW: a key never changes what it does. A face is paint. config.ts strips `on`, `actions`, `callEndpoint`, URLs outside the art host and anything that reads typed text from skin input, and the renderer refuses them again. App Review 4.4.1.
Key positions come only from the tree the server already builds. A skin cannot move, add or remove a key.

pressCases.why: Today's effect, and the fallback for everything else.
Scale and lift, with the server's numbers.
An unknown kind falls back to fade, exactly as Reduce Motion does.
400 ms at most. A press effect is visual only: it runs AFTER the commit and never delays insertText.

One press block goes to both phones, so one clamp holds for both: 0.9 to 1.12. On a key about 32 pt wide with the usual 6 pt gap, 1.12 grows about 1.9 pt a side and stays inside its half of the gap. Before this, iPhone clamped at 1.4 and Android at 1.1, so the same skin felt different on each.
-6 to 6, about half the row gap, in points on iPhone and dp on Android.
The server writes ms, scale and dy explicitly into every pop, so no phone default ever decides how a skin looks. The two renderers have different built-in defaults.

state.down: eases to (scale, dy) over ms and HOLDS
state.up: settles over ms from wherever it is

pressCases.why: A pressed STATE, not a release bounce, and the same on both phones: iPhone already ships one (KBPress.begin at keyTouchDown, end at keyTouchUp). A release-only bounce would make the same skin feel different on each phone, and on the commit-on-down path a glow that appears only after the lift reads as lag — the letter is already in the field. The key's own view is never transformed: the paint moves and the hit rect does not.

budgetCases.why: 64 faced keys per config. Above that the extras keep their plain titles.

budgetCases.keep: 3 animated keys; the rest draw their mark at t = 0
budgetCases.why: At most 3 keys animate, enforced IN THE VIEW. A non-animated faced key never starts a CADisplayLink — each TulmiMarkView owns one, so thirty of them idling would cost frames for nothing.

budgetCases.keep: under 6 MB of live images; the rest draw the flat colour
budgetCases.why: The live-image budget counts width x height x 4 for images attached to LIVE key views. The 12-image cache cap does not help here: it only evicts dictionary entries, not what is on screen.
At most 2 hooked fonts per keyboard config, TTF or OTF, 300 KB each, registered at runtime. A font that fails to register means the design's next font, then sans.

guardCases.why: The trial marker is the config's sha, set when a config AND its prefetched art are applied, and cleared only on a CLEAN FINISH (iOS viewDidDisappear, Android onFinishInputView) — never on a 20 second timer, so a memory death once art and animated keys have built up is still counted. Two strikes on a skinned config switch that sha to plain mode: face, press, fontFamily and art are ignored; the tree and the colours stay, because those are today's features.
Plain mode also tells the server, which then sends the unskinned tree to that device.

Two more strikes, or an unskinned config that still dies, fall back to today's behaviour: drop the cached config and use the bundled snapshot. That snapshot stays UNSKINNED and unchanged in this build, so the no-Full-Access keyboard and the guard's last resort never depend on new code.
Android has no crash guard at all today. This is new code in TulmiKeyboardService.kt: a marker in the tulmi_kb prefs, the sha of config_json, and two strikes.

privacyCases.how: Type a hundred characters and switch layouts five times, with a proxy log running.
privacyCases.why: EVERY fetch happens at keyboard open: the config (TTL 60 s), then one batch of every art file and font in the manifest. Nothing is fetched on a key press or a layout switch, so no request can be tied to a keystroke even when the art differs per key.
No typed text ever leaves the device. The token is there so the server can apply the person's own skin pick, nothing else.
There is no per-key press counting, ever. The speed counters already exist; they are only tagged with the skin id so a skin that regresses can be stopped.
